questions.q: What question do auditing and lineage columns exist to answer?
options: Which load run put a given row there, when, and from which source
What the customer's current shipping address is
How many total sales occurred last quarter
Whether a table has a primary key
questions.explain: Audit columns are metadata about the ETL process itself, so a row's origin and load history can always be traced on demand.

questions.q: What does the LoadDate column actually represent?
options: The timestamp the row was loaded, not any business date on the row itself
The date the customer placed their order
The date the table was originally created
The scheduled date of the next load
questions.explain: LoadDate is ETL metadata — it answers when the row was loaded, distinct from any business date the row's actual data carries.

questions.q: Why is a SourceSystem column especially important?
options: Because more than one upstream system often feeds the same staging or warehouse table, and rows need to be traceable to the right one
Because SQL Server requires it to enforce foreign keys
Because it replaces the need for a BatchID column
Because it stores the customer's preferred communication channel
questions.explain: When a warehouse merges data from multiple source systems (e.g., a legacy system and its replacement), SourceSystem is what lets you tell which one a given row actually came from.

questions.q: What does a BatchID column let you do that LoadDate alone cannot as cleanly?
options: Identify and select every row loaded together in one specific run, for debugging or reprocessing
Automatically fix any data quality issue in that batch
Prevent the batch from ever being reloaded
Convert loosely typed staging columns into their final warehouse types
questions.explain: BatchID groups every row from a single load run under one identifier, letting you isolate exactly that run's rows without guessing based on timestamps alone.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes what a lineage column should NOT be used for?
options: As a business attribute or measure that a report is built around, such as treating LoadDate as an order's ship date
As a way to trace a warehouse row back to the load run that populated it
As a column present on both staging and warehouse tables
As metadata that helps debug a specific ETL run
questions.explain: Audit columns are ETL metadata, not business data — mixing them into a model's actual measures or dimension attributes blurs a distinction that keeps the model easy to query correctly.
